_note: Protocol = the paper's R code 1:1 (see the YAML header): measured 2026-08-26 on the refactor/lean-fit branch. Paper Sec. 5.3. Counterfactuals are analytic. The Fig. 6 errors are at x_obs in the SCM's raw units, (2, 1.5, 5.0875, -0.5) = noise (2, 1.5, 1.4, -1) pushed through the SCM; the R code's xObs.csv is that point divided by CAREFL's sample sds (6.0104, 1.9114), (2, 1.5, 0.8465, -0.2616); the paper prints (2, 1.5, 0.81, -0.28), slightly off it. Held-out rows are scored next to it because one point is a noisy yardstick. The R run trained on CAREFL's own X.csv with val = train; this repository draws 2500 rows from the same SCM and a separate 5000-row validation draw. Optimization settled 2026-09-03 after measuring BOTH protocols on the fixed benchmark data: 3000 epochs @ lr 0.002 (kept) beats the reference's 7000 @ 0.001 on four of six held-out counterfactual MAEs (x4 0.123/0.097/0.122 vs 0.204/0.134/0.162) and on x4's validation NLL (1.393 vs 1.419) — the reference's anneal steps on the SUMMED val NLL, so x4's overfit hides behind x3's improvement; the reference wins only the single-observation Fig. 6 curve (x4 0.59 vs 0.77), which the dip analysis below shows is draw noise. Held-out beats one noisy point. The fig6 bounds kept from the reference-run tightening still hold here (band 1.7-1.9x). The residual x4 dip near alpha=0 was root-caused 2026-09-03 and is finite-sample tail-quantile variance at the reference's own n_train = 2500, NOT protocol or init: invariant to epochs (3000 vs 7000), to val=train vs held-out, and to init seeds 7/8/9 (max err 0.586/0.601/0.610); mechanism pinned at the quantile level (the observed noise sits at the Laplace 12% quantile — the fitted conditional's 12% quantile errs +0.27 at the sparse observation region x1=2, ~190 nearby rows, and -0.19 in the dense middle, and the obs-anchored curve inherits the difference); magnitude moves with the DATA draw (err@alpha0 0.54/0.31/0.43 over dgp seeds 42/43/44). Conditional medians are within 0.15 of truth across the grid. The paper's single-run Fig. 6 sits inside this band in its standardized units (~0.29 on a 3-unit axis).
